summary.text: A 77-year-old woman with hypertension, hypothyroidism and dyslipidaemia presented with chest discomfort/breathlessness, stable vitals and an unremarkable examination, without reported recent stress or recreational drug use. Troponin rose from 755 to 815 ng/L; ECG showed anterolateral ST depression and initial echo showed EF 30% with mid/apical abnormalities. She was treated for presumed ACS; coronary angiography showed no significant CAD. One-week CMR showed midventricular oedema and circumferential hypokinesis with basal/apical sparing, supporting documented midventricular Takotsubo diagnosis. Perfusion/stress CMR was not completed at her request. A 4 cm ascending aorta remained under follow-up. LGE-negative imaging and the related myocarditis exclusion conflict with a discussion statement that identifying LGE was not feasible; these claims remain review-only. Authors also discuss cocaine-related ischemia, neurogenic injury and pheochromocytoma-associated dysfunction as differentials judged unlikely, without documenting them as diagnoses. Repeat stress echo one month later showed normal LV function, no reversible ischemia and TTC resolution; subsequent symptoms/exercise tolerance recovered. Dual antiplatelets were stopped while bisoprolol and ramipril 1.25 mg daily continued.
